### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**16** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/observability/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/observability/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f722411eddac2c3e34235cd7a5ba1ccdda4d40d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e41bcf21d8769eafb528451a68904ac1b309d150` — the merge of head `80855b22b02063419c2db2e6dab9bb9b2983eb0c` into base `f722411eddac2c3e34235cd7a5ba1ccdda4d40d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e41bcf21d8769eafb528451a68904ac1b309d150 && git checkout e41bcf21d8769eafb528451a68904ac1b309d150
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f722411eddac2c3e34235cd7a5ba1ccdda4d40d4 80855b22b02063419c2db2e6dab9bb9b2983eb0c && git checkout -B drift-repro f722411eddac2c3e34235cd7a5ba1ccdda4d40d4 && git merge --no-ff 80855b22b02063419c2db2e6dab9bb9b2983eb0c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f722411eddac2c3e34235cd7a5ba1ccdda4d40d4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `80855b22b02063419c2db2e6dab9bb9b2983eb0c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #37658 (body, triage, unblock, claim, os-dev report, claim amendment), PR #37716 (body, 7 files, net diff against `main`), N4 of the contract record on PR #37652, and the head's 73 check-runs (62 success, 11 skipped, none failed). The required set is green on this head: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1-10/10, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Validate Package Dependencies, Check Changeset, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Test UI 1-16/16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI and Dogfood Regression Gate. `Security-touching: yes` because the diff adds a third copy of the field-name matcher that decides which object-cause fields an operator log withholds, and it adds content to what reaches operator log sinks.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Log record shape, `ConsoleLogger` / `JsonLogger` `error()` and `fatal()`: a new optional `causes` field beside `error` and `stack`.** Right. `errorFields` builds `{ error, stack, ...(causes.length ? { causes } : {}) }`. The key order and values are those of the old literal `{ error: error.message, stack: error.stack }`, so an error with no `cause` (also `cause: null`, `cause: undefined`, or a throwing `cause` getter) serializes byte-identically on both loggers. The per-logger CONTROL test pins the omission. The other four levels are untouched.
- **The private `causeChain` copy against `faultCauseChain` (`packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`).** Faithful, read line by line. It has the same loop: `seen` is seeded with the outer error, the cycle check runs before the depth check, the limit is 5 (`CAUSE_DEPTH_LIMIT`), and the three marker strings are identical (cycle, `truncated after 5 links`, unreadable link). `causeOf` is guarded, and `causeLine` renders `name: message` with stack omitted when it is empty. The string and JSON object-cause branches with their `String()` fallback match. The field-name matcher (`DEFAULT_REDACTED_WORDS`, `tokenizeFieldName`, `singularizeWord`, `CONCATENATED_SECRET_QUALIFIERS`, `isQualifiedConcatenation`, `containsWordRun`, `fieldWordsMatchPattern`) is a verbatim copy. The 31 qualifiers form the same set in all five places (core `logger.ts`, types, observability, and the two fixture lists). The one signature difference is `causeChain(error: Error)` with no `isRedacted` parameter, against `faultCauseChain(thrown: unknown, isRedacted = default)`. It is behaviour-neutral, because the loggers have no redact config to pass.
- **Never-throw contract.** Held. `errorFields` runs in `error()` / `fatal()`, outside `emit`'s try. Every read it adds is guarded (`causeOf` try, per-link try), and the `error.message` / `error.stack` reads it keeps were already outside the try on `main`.
- **Parity binding, 12 fixtures × 2 loggers, `toEqual(faultCauseChain(error))`.** Right, with one gap (N2). The fixtures pin the depth limit (a 9-cause chain, and the limit imported from `@objectstack/types` in the depth test), the cycle marker, the unreadable-link marker, the throwing getter, string, object and unserializable causes, and the whole-word field-name rule including all 31 glued qualifiers. A change to any branch the fixtures reach, in either copy, reds a case.
- **Public surface.** Unchanged apart from the log field. `src/index.ts` is untouched: no export is added or removed. `loggers.ts` imports nothing new (only `import type { Logger }`). `dependencies` is still `@objectstack/spec` alone.
- **Accept-set.** No accept-set change. The diff touches no schema, validator or parser.
- **Test-only edges.** Right. `@objectstack/types` is a `devDependency`. `@objectstack/types` depends on `@objectstack/spec` only, so the workspace graph has no cycle (Validate Package Dependencies is green). `vitest.config.ts` is not in the package's `files` (`dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`). Its alias is anchored, `^@objectstack/types$` to `../types/src/index.ts`, which re-exports `server-fault-log.js`. The preset's one setting, `disableConsoleIntercept: true`, is spelled in place, verbatim. The lockfile hunk is 3 lines, the new devDependency link in the observability importer and nothing else.
- **Core test (`packages/core/src/logger-error-cause.test.ts`).** Test-only. It adds one fixture and a control. `ObjectLogger` and `logServerFault` are unchanged, as the claim requires.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — confirmed. The change is an additive, optional field on a log record that already merges arbitrary caller `meta`, so the record had no closed shape and no existing field changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, because nothing a metadata author writes changes. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The changeset is `'@objectstack/observability': patch`, it carries both bare lines, and so does the PR body (Check Changeset is green). The card's original `Clause-②: no` was corrected by the claim amendment, in line with the seat's reading on PR #37652. That correction is right.

Existing parsers of `JsonLogger` output: a line-per-record JSON reader sees one more key, and only on a caused error. Nothing breaks unless a consumer validates records against a closed schema, which a record merging free `meta` could never have satisfied. One precedence detail: a caller-supplied `meta.causes` is now overridden when the error has a chain. This is the same precedence `meta.error` and `meta.stack` already had, and `git grep` finds no caller that passes `causes` in logger meta. Lines grow by up to six stacks, as `ObjectLogger` lines already do.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none raised.
- `security_findings`: the dev reported none. Nothing contrary was found in the diff.
- `deviations`: none. The claim amendment widens the named file surface to `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`, all inside the claim's "devDependency for the parity test" allowance. No runtime edge was added.
- Out-of-scope finding (hand-copied fixture lists): answered as N1 below. It is real and does not block.
- N4 of PR #37652: closed as written. That record asked for "one fixture with each qualifier glued to a default word". `GLUED_QUALIFIERS` glues all 31 to `key`, and each `${q}key` is a single token that matches only through its own qualifier: no compound path, no singular form, no other default word as a suffix. A qualifier removed from, or changed in, either copy therefore reds a parity case. The control proves the fixture currently exercises all 31 against `faultCauseChain`. The same fixture rides in observability's parity block.
- Test UI (11/16): unreachable from this diff. It failed once, at `ui/packages/auth/src/__tests__/AuthProvider.test.tsx` on a render count, and is green on rerun on this head (job 140239738628, completed 2026-11-27T00:50Z). The diff has no `ui/` path, no file under `ui/` imports `@objectstack/observability`, `ui/packages/auth` depends on `@objectstack/spec` alone, and the only lockfile change is the observability importer.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff touches no data path, no query, and no id materialisation or in-app join.

Findings:

- N1 (nit): the drift guard is one-directional. A qualifier or default word that is removed or changed in any copy reds parity. One added to a single copy (to `CONCATENATED_SECRET_QUALIFIERS` or to `DEFAULT_REDACTED_WORDS` in types, core or observability) fails nothing until the hand-copied fixture lists grow too. The dev disclosed this, and core has the same shape. A follow-up could derive the fixture from one exported list.
- N2 (nit): two branches that all three copies share have no fixture. One is an `Error` cause with an empty `stack` (the stack-omitted branch of `causeLine`). The other is a chain that continues through a non-`Error` object cause that itself carries `cause`. The copies agree there today on read. A drift in only one of them would pass the parity block.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37658-observability-cause-chain`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**
